description.narrative: Establish solid and strategic links to involve key political, civil society and economic actors, to promote an informed understanding of the importance of free competition in the economic development and the country prosperity. And support an effective adoption of a competition law

Etablera solida och strategiska länkar för att involvera viktiga politiska, civila samhället och ekonomiska aktörer, för att främja en välgrundad förståelse för vikten av fri konkurrens för den ekonomiska utvecklingen och landets välstånd. Och stödja ett effektivt antagande av en konkurrenslag

Overall Objective:
To promote the application and understanding of the "Competition Law" in Guatemala, strengthening technical capacity of decision makers, involved actors and promoting a culture of competition that encourages economic efficiency and positioning the country as a destination for foreign direct investment.
Specific objectives:
To contribute to generate consensus and capacity building based on the experience and knowledge of experts to improve the effectiveness of competition legislation.
To analyze current challenges and opportunities in the application of the Competition Law in order to propose effective ways of going forward.
Promote the involvement of various interested actors, including experts, companies, civil society and consumers, in the formulation of policies to promote competition.

description.narrative:
Advocacy work and communication process with different actors of civil society, government, academy, media, among others, made by Asociacion Consejo Nacional Empresarial -CNE- supported by the Swedish Embassy in Guatemala, contributed to the approval of the Competition Law on November 19th 2024. To achieve this result, many important activities were developed, as mentioned as follow:
The Technical Committee for Competition (CompiteGuate) was created. This Committee has been an inter-institutional and multidisciplinary initiative aimed at promoting an evidence-based discussion for the approval and implementation of a regulatory framework for competition that ensures economic efficiency. CompiteGuate is integrated by 11 members, between civil organizations, government representatives, academy, international experts and CNE.
Approximately 15 events and meetings were organized to provide opportunities for direct dialogue between the law's advocates, legislators and private sector representative. These events were planned and designed to inform, answer questions, and build relationships around the law's approval process. The events were held in Guatemala City and in the departments of Quetzaltenango, Sacatepequez, Alta Verapaz and Peten.
Strategic allies were sought within and outside the political sphere to share the objectives of promoting competition. These alliances included civil society organizations, academics, entrepreneurs, and other relevant actors.
A round of approaches was carried out with the leaders of the Congress of the Republic of Guatemala, members of the Presidential Commission for the Competition Law, Ministry of Economy, Ministry of Finance, Vice Ministry of Investment and Competition, SEGEPLAN, PRONACOM, among others.
A Communication strategy was developed. Messages disseminated in the communication campaign helped to inform about the benefits of the Competition Law in order to reduce the misinformation. In terms of key actions, an audience mapping was carried out, which facilitated interaction with various sectors: civil society (both current and new followers), the business sector, the public sector, and academia (Guatemalan universities).
The Competition Observatory started its operation inside the COMPITEGUATE (Committee for Competition technical table). In this phase, COMPITEGUATE has fulfilled some of the functions of the observatory, as it has generated information for decision-makers throughout the process for the approval of the competition law, as well as providing inputs for the drafting of the regulations. In the next phase of the project, a series of regulations and agreements will need to be developed under this component to operationalize the observatory in the new Competition Superintendence, when this entity is created.
